Alejandro Frery: Born in Mendoza, Argentina, Professor Frery earned degrees in electronic and electrical engineering, applied mathematics, and applied computing in Argentina and Brazil. His research spans data visualisation, statistical computing, and stochastic modelling, with applications in signal and image processing and networks. Since 2020, he has been Professor of Statistics and Data Science at Victoria University of Wellington in New Zealand. Professor Frery has held several leadership roles in the IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Society, including Editor-in-Chief of IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters and Vice President for Publications. He received the IEEE GRSS Regional Leader Award in 2018.
Paul A. Rosen: Paul A. Rosen is currently Project Scientist for NASA-ISRO synthetic aperture radar mission (NISAR) at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and is a JPL Fellow and Senior Research Scientist. He received the 2026 NASA Public Leadership Medal for his role in formulating the NISAR mission and championing its science capabilities throughout the mission development. He was the study coordinator for NASA’s Surface Deformation and Change Decadal Survey Architecture Study from 2018 to 2026. Until 2012, he was the manager of the Radar Science and Engineering Section and Project Scientist for the DESDynI Mission concept at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. He has been active in understanding the phenomenology and scientific potentials of interferometric SAR and has led research initiatives in data analysis and the development of software tools and techniques. Dr. Rosen was the team leader for Algorithm Development and Verification on the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission, for which he received NASA's Exceptional Service Medal (2001) and NASA's Exceptional Achievement Medal (2002). As a graduate student, post-doc, and early career research scientist, Dr. Rosen studied resonance phenomena in Saturn’s rings using radio occultation data from the NASA Voyager mission. Dr. Rosen is a visiting faculty member and lecturer at the Division of Geological and Planetary Sciences and the Electrical Engineering Department at Caltech. He is a member of the American Geophysical Union, and recipient of its Geodesy Section Ivan I. Mueller Award for Distinguished Service and Leadership. He is also a Fellow of the IEEE. He is an author on over 60 journal and book chapter publications, and over 200 conference papers.
Anabella Ferral: Dr. Anabella Ferral is an Adjunct Researcher at CONICET and Titular Professor at the National University of Córdoba. Her career combines physical chemistry, environmental sciences, remote sensing, and geospatial analysis, with a strong focus on water resources using satellite data. She is Associate Editor of IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine and was appointed IEEE-GRSS Distinguished Lecturer for the 2025–2026 period. She has authored and co-authored numerous peer-reviewed scientific publications in high-impact international journals and IEEE conferences. She has supervised doctoral, master’s, and undergraduate theses in geomatics, environmental management, and spatial information applications. Her current research integrates satellite technologies, environmental monitoring, and emerging nanotechnologies to address water pollution, ecosystem degradation, and climate-related challenges in the context of the SDGs 2030. She is an active early-career member of GEOAQUAWATCH.
Gerardo Di Martino: Gerardo Di Martino (Senior Member, IEEE) is Associate Professor of Electromagnetic Fields in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology at the University of Naples Federico II, Italy. He holds the Italian national habilitation as Full Professor of Electromagnetic Fields. His main research interests are in the field of microwave remote sensing and electromagnetics, with focus on electromagnetic scattering modeling, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system and data modeling, information extraction from SAR and polarimetric SAR data, SAR data simulation and physical-based benchmarking approaches. In the last years, he has also worked on the development of models for Earth Observation through Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R). He is co-Editor of the book “Maritime Surveillance with Synthetic Aperture Radar”, published by IET in 2020. He authored more than 150 papers, of which about 50 published in refereed journals. Prof. Di Martino has a broad teaching experience, spanning from basic Electromagnetic Fields bachelor classes to advanced Remote Sensing master classes. He has been invited as speaker at top-tier international symposia, such as IGARSS and PIERS, where he has also organized and chaired several sessions. He is co-organizer and presenter of technical tutorials at IEEE IGARSS 2024, IEEE ICSIDP 2024, and IET IRC 2025. He is the founding Lead Editor of the IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Society (GRSS) Section within IEEE Access, and an Associate Editor of the IEEE Journal of Selected Topics on Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing.
Ryo Natsuaki: Ryo Natsuaki (Student member 2011-2014, Regular member 2015-2020, Senior member 2021-present) received B. S., M. S. and Ph. D. degrees in electrical engineering from The University of Tokyo, Japan in 2009, 2011 and 2014, respectively. He was Aerospace Project Research Associate of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), Tsukuba, Japan from 2014 to 2017. He was also a guest scientist with Microwaves and Radar Institute, German Aerospace Center (DLR), Oberpfaffenhofen, Germany from 2018 to 2020 under JSPS Overseas Research Fellowships. He is currently an Associate Professor with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Systems, The University of Tokyo, Japan. His research interests include active remote sensing with synthetic aperture radar (SAR). He is also a member of the Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers (IEICE), Japan and American Geophysical Union (AGU). He currently serves as an associate editor of IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (IEEE TGRS), a secretary of IEICE technical committee on Electromagnetic Theory (EMT). He is also a technical committee member of Frequency Allocations in Remote Sensing (FARS) and Remote sensing Environment, Analysis and Climate Technologies Technical Committee (REACT) in GRSS. He was a publicity chair of IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS) 2019 and secretary of IEEE GRSS Japan chapter from 2014 to 2017 as well as a secretary of IEICE technical committee on Space, Aeronautical and Navigational Electronics (SANE) from 2017 to 2022.
Francescopaolo Sica: Francescopaolo Sica (Senior Member, IEEE) is Deputy Head of the Chair of Earth Observation at the University of the Bundeswehr Munich, Germany. He received his Ph.D. in Information Engineering in 2016 and has held research positions at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA). His work focuses on SAR signal and image processing, with an emphasis on integrating deep learning methods for enhanced data processing and analysis. Dr. Sica serves as Co-Chair of the Benchmarking Working Group of the IEEE GRSS IADF Technical Committee.
Rajeev Jyoti: Rajeev Jyoti is the Director (Technical) at the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), where he leads initiatives to strengthen India's commercial space ecosystem, promote Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) in Earth Observation, and facilitate private-sector participation in space exploration. He joined ISRO in 1987 and served for over 36 years at the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad, contributing to the design and development of microwave payloads and advanced antenna systems for more than 25 satellites. His notable contributions include RISAT-1, RISAT-1A, NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR), Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 radar altimeters, and India's first constellation of three X-band SAR imaging satellites. He is a co-inventor of 14 patents and has authored over 170 technical papers. He has received several prestigious honours, including the IEEE Indian Council Outstanding Industry Award (2020) and ISRO Performance Excellence Award (2015). He is a Fellow of INAE, Aeronautical Society of India and IETE, and a Senior Member of IEEE. Before joining IN-SPACe, he served as Associate Director of the Space Applications Centre, ISRO.
A. S. Kiran Kumar: Shri A. S. Kiran Kumar is a distinguished Indian space scientist and former Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), having served as Secretary, Department of Space, and Chairman of the Space Commission from January 2015 to January 2018. He joined ISRO in 1975 and has over four decades of experience in satellite technology, Earth Observation, remote sensing and space exploration. He made significant contributions to the development of advanced electro-optical imaging sensors and satellite payloads, particularly for the Chandrayaan-1 and Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) missions. Before becoming ISRO Chairman, he served as Director of the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad. In recognition of his outstanding contributions to space science and technology, he was conferred the Padma Shri in 2014, the International von Karman Wings Award in 2018 and the Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur by the Government of France in 2019. He is a Fellow of several prestigious professional institutions, including the Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE).
Prakash Chauhan: Dr. Prakash Chauhan is a distinguished space scientist and Director of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), ISRO, Hyderabad. He joined the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in 1991 at the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad, and has over three decades of experience in remote sensing, Earth Observation, geosciences, atmospheric and oceanographic studies, and natural resource management. He has made significant contributions to planetary exploration through India's Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-2 missions and served as the Principal Investigator of the Imaging Infrared Spectrometer (IIRS) onboard Chandrayaan-2, which provided important evidence of water molecules on the lunar surface. Prior to becoming Director of NRSC, he served as Director of the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun, from April 2018. His contributions include pioneering research in ocean colour, aerosol remote sensing, air quality monitoring, disaster risk reduction and planetary science. He has authored more than 150 peer-reviewed research papers and received several prestigious honours, including the Asia-Pacific Regional Excellence in Space Award (2023), ISRO Merit Award (2010), Satish Dhawan Award (2016) and Prof. P. R. Pisharoty Memorial Award (2004). He is a Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), Indian Society of Remote Sensing (ISRS) and Indian Social Science Academy, and a Corresponding Member of the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA).
C. V. N. Rao: Dr. Ch. V. N. Narasimha Rao is a distinguished scientist and Director of the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Ahmedabad, having assumed charge on 1 August 2026. He joined ISRO in 1989 and has over 37 years of experience in the development of advanced microwave remote sensing technologies for Earth observation and planetary missions. He has made significant contributions to the design and development of several state-of-the-art microwave payloads, including C-band Synthetic Aperture Radars for RISAT-1, EOS-04 and EOS-09; Ku-band Scatterometers for Oceansat-2, SCATSAT-1 and EOS-06; RISAT-2B series payloads; Ka-band radar altimeters for Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3; and the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission. He has also played a key role in promoting indigenous technology development, industry participation and self-reliance in advanced space technologies. He holds a Ph.D. from Dhirubhai Ambani Institute of Information and Communication Technology (DAIICT), Gandhinagar. He has authored over 150 peer-reviewed research publications, received more than 500 citations and holds six patents. He is a Member of the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA), Senior Member of IEEE, and Life Member of the Astronautical Society of India (ASI), Indian Society of Remote Sensing (ISRS) and Indian Society of Systems for Science and Engineering (ISSE).
T. M. Balakrishnan Nair: Dr. T. M. Balakrishnan Nair is the Director of the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, Hyderabad. He is one of the founding members of INCOIS and has over 30 years of research experience in operational oceanography, ocean observation systems, wave modelling and marine services. He has played a pivotal role in establishing India's real-time ocean observation networks and developing operational ocean forecast, early warning and advisory services for India and other Indian Ocean Rim countries. His contributions include developing ocean information services for disaster management, shipping, fisheries, ports, offshore energy and other blue-economy sectors. He holds a Ph.D. in Marine Science from Mangalore University and an M.Sc. in Marine Geology and Oceanography from Cochin University of Science and Technology. He has authored over 160 scientific publications and is a Fellow of the Telangana Academy of Sciences. His prestigious recognitions include the National Geoscience Award (2014), National Maritime Search and Rescue Award (2024) and Swadeshi Shastra Puraskaram (2025). He also serves in several international scientific leadership positions, including Chair of the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS) under the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) of UNESCO.
Saibun Tjuatja: Dr. Saibun Tjuatja is the 2026 President of the IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Society (GRSS) and an Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering at The University of Texas at Arlington, USA. He received his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Texas at Arlington and joined its faculty in 1993. His research interests include microwave remote sensing, electromagnetic scattering and emission from random media, signal processing, and inversion algorithms, with applications in snow, glaciers, sea ice and humanitarian demining. He has been actively associated with IEEE GRSS since 1992, contributing to its technical committees, conferences and publications. He served as General Co-Chair of IGARSS 2017 in Texas and as Executive Vice President of GRSS before assuming the presidency in January 2025. As GRSS President in 2026, his vision focuses on enhancing the membership experience, broadening global participation, and extending the impact of geoscience and remote sensing innovations to industry and society.
